summary: This work demonstrates key elements of patch-based surface-code logical processing on a 107-qubit superconducting processor, implementing code-deformation and lattice-surgery primitives (merge, split, expansion, shrinkage, domain walls, twist defects) and composing them into a Clifford-generating set of logical gates (H, S, CNOT) on distance-3 rotated surface-code patches with multi-round syndrome extraction and neural-network decoding. All operations are performed without post-selection, advancing superconducting surface-code experiments from protected logical memory to active, measurement-based logical operations.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires logical operations that manipulate encoded information while maintaining error-correction protection, but the locality constraints of surface codes restrict transversal gate implementations. Code deformation and lattice surgery provide a measurement-based route to such operations through reconfigurable patch geometries and boundaries.
method: On the Zuchongzhi 3.2 processor with average 1Q error $1.01 \times 10^{-3}$, CZ error $5.06 \times 10^{-3}$, and readout error $1.11 \times 10^{-2}$, the authors implemented logical state routing via lattice-surgery teleportation and code deformation, logical CNOT via ancilla-mediated parity measurements using a $7 \times 7$ footprint and 6 QEC cycles, logical H via geometric patch rotation combined with a Hadamard domain wall using a $3 \times 5$ footprint and 6 cycles, and logical S via gate teleportation with fault-tolerant $|+i\rangle$ ancilla using a $3 \times 7$ footprint and 4–5 cycles. All circuits use distance-3 patches and neural-network decoding of the syndrome record.
result: Decoded logical state fidelities for routing: $0.908$–$0.911$ for Z-basis states, $0.841$–$0.863$ for X-basis states. Logical CNOT Bell-state fidelities: $0.550$–$0.624$, all above the separability bound of $0.5$; average PTM fidelity $0.643(2)$. Logical H gate: PTM elements $R_{X \to Z} = 0.796(2)$, $R_{Z \to X} = 0.784(5)$, $R_{Y \to Y} = -0.546(4)$; average gate fidelity $0.854(1)$. Logical S gate: PTM elements $R_{X \to Y} = 0.589(3)$, $R_{Y \to -X} = -0.587(3)$, $R_{Z \to Z} = 0.901(3)$; average gate fidelity $0.846(1)$. Circuit-level distance verification confirms all distance-3 gates are distance-preserving; simulations indicate logical-error suppression with distance enters a pronounced regime when physical error rates are reduced to $\approx 50\%$ of present values.
